description.narrative: 1. Number of market vendors trained in, and who are evidenced to apply improved business management practices 2. Number of market vendors trained in, and who are evidenced to access financial services (measured through signup to services) 3. Number of market vendors/ farmers trained in, and engaging in improved agribusiness practices to increase agricultural productivity. This includes identified vendor-farmers accessing Agricultural Services or Farmer Networks , or demonstrating adoption of the improved, climate and disaster resilient, agricultural methods taught as part of the training. 4. Number of market vendors/ farmers trained in, and engaging in improved agribusiness practices to increase agricultural profitability. This includes identified vendor-farmers showing continued use of improved business management practices, or demonstrating adoption of value adding methods taught as part of the training for product diversification.

• Selected women market vendors interviewed and reported improved economic status based on increased income, savings, or financial capital (loans, credit, savings, investments) • women market vendors have demonstrated improved socioeconomic security • women market vendors demonstrate agency in financial decision-making in their business and households. • women market vendors are accessing gender-inclusive financial and social services. • women market vendors have increased business and financial skills, such as starting and maintain savings and recording-keeping. women market vendors have developed digital literacy, using online platforms to strengthen their business, like marketing their produce or strengthening and maintaining their network via social media platforms. • women market vendors have diversified market business due to Covid 19 Pandemic
PARTNERSHIP - IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECT INTERVENTIONS
This year, key partnerships were established with organisations for the direct implementation of Outcome 2 project activities. The various organisations selected have technical expertise in empowering urban and rural women market vendors; developing capacities, strengthening institutions, delivering services and training to market vendors; ensuring there is continuous learning and effective knowledge management. The following partners were selected and partnerships strengthened through project implementation: • Government Partners: Partnerships with government as core partnership for sustainability of the outcome 2 implementation. The primary partnerships are with local-level government in the four target countries. Partnerships has been formalized within the four countries.
• MVA Partners: Strengthened collaboration with the 21 MVAs across the 4 countries. The MVAs are entry points to selected the rural women market vendors and farmers to attend the financial literacy trainings, business management trainings and the agriculture value addition trainings and protective cropping trainings. The MVAs also supported the planning, coordination and implementation of Outcome 2 activities.
• Private Sector Partners: UNDP continued to strengthen and maintain close coordination and collaboration with ANZ Pacific, Vodafone Fiji, Digicel Pacific. The partnership includes support from the financial institution and digital enterprises to help create market access, and deliver services for women market vendors.
• UN Agencies: Strengthened partnership between UNWomen, UNDP and UNCDF on financial literacy and financial skills training and Parametric microinsurance ; FAO for agricultural support.
Output 2.1: Market vendors have increased agency over financial decision making in their business (vending and other businesses).
? Fiji: Supported urban and rural women market vendors through the Money Minded Training conducted by ANZ Bank. The training included topics such as planning for the future, making money last until next pay day, needs and wants, being assertive (learning to say No) and commitment. 668 market vendors from Suva, Nausori, Sigatoka, Rakiraki, Nadi, Namaka, Tavua, Ba, Lautoka, Levuka, Savusavu, Labasa and Kadavu participated in the training.(440 women,188 men, 40 youth, 12 people living with disability & Household Approach -35 couples , 5 village Headmen). Post evaluation at the end of the training indicated, that 145 women are practicing record keeping, contributing to improved savings behaviour, compared to 15 have opened new bank accounts and 4 couples have confirmed that women have increased agency over financial decision making in their business.
Fiji: ? Two market business fair was implemented in Kadavu and Levuka , resulting in 175 rural market ( 95 women, 30 men and 15 youths) having access to financial and social services. The BSP Bank, Westpac Bank, CCSLA, Unit Trust, Vodafone, Digicel, FNPF , Fiji Revenue & Customs. 20 rural women market vendors have opened savings with Unit Trust, 45 rural women market vendors have opened their voluntary FNPF Accounts and 10 have opened voluntary accounts for their children, 106 rural women and men were able to TIN letters, and open accounts with FNPF and Unit Trust Fiji, 15 rural women market vendors opened MPAISA Accounts with Vodafone, and 10 rural women opened MYCASH account with Digicel. 35 rural women visited the market fair, and access general enquiries on opening bank account, resulting in 3 opening bank accounts for their children’s savings.
? Supported 250 Municipal market vendors ( Suva (50),Kadavu (50), Levuka (50), Savusavu (50) and Labasa (50) access Personal Protective Equipments for Covid 19 Pandemic preventative measures, resulting in good health and hygiene practices, extra precautionary measures undertaken by the market vendors.
? Supported 45 rural market vendors (25 women, 20 men) access the Parametric Micro -insurance products, resulting in 5 market vendors (3 women, 2 men) signing up for the Parametric Micro-insurance with CCSLA. Lessons learnt, confirmed the need to create more awareness on the Parametric Insurance. Most farmers prefer to signup individually rather than as a group as it can be a high risk.
Output 2.3: Market vendors business is improved and more resilient as a result of an increase in business and financial skills (savings and recording) and access to digital literacy and online platforms
Fiji: ? Supported 40 market vendors (25 women, 15 men) to participate in the Digital Literacy Training. The 40 market vendors from Suva, Nausori, Nadi, Namaka, Rakiraki, Ba, Tavua, Labasa, Savusavu, Levuka and Kadavu accessed the Makete Platform to promote their market produce. 10 women were able to open Zoom Account, 2 created facebook accounts, and 40 market vendors all accessing MAKETE platform for the first time. Lessons learnt, confirmed the need for more trainings on Digital Literacy.
? 45 market vendors (10 women,6 men, 4 youth, 2 people living with disability & Household Approach -4 couples)from Suva, Nausori, Sigatoka, Rakiraki, Nadi, Namaka, Tavua, Ba, Lautoka, Levuka, Savusavu, Labasa and Kadavu that were trained in Financial literacy training indicated the need to expand their business and financial skills in preparing a proposal, business plan and also alternative streams for earning extra income to supplement their farm business.
Output 2.4: Increase in economic and sustainable livelihoods through improved resilient and climate smart agricultural practices and value adding.
Fiji: ? Supported 235 rural women market vendor farmers (145 men and 77 women, 30 youths, 2 people living with disability) participate in the Value Addition training, Farm Management and Poultry Farming Training in Kadavu. The training ensured the farmers are equipped with basic value addition knowledge and skills, that will increase economic, sustainable and practicable livelihood options brining increase in income for the farmers.
? Supported 40 farmers ( 25 men and 15 women) from Nausori Highland through the Protective Cropping Training, resulting in increasing the capacity of rural women market vendor farmers to produce high quality vegetables in protected cropping systems. The training also focused on the development of value chains to connect farmers using these systems to high value markets for Fresh vegetables
? Supported 300 farmers (145 women, and 155 men) in Kadavu, resulting in sustainable livelihood through food security and sufficient consistent supply of produce to meet the demands of the people living within Kadavu Province.
